evidence: The deposition of thin PTO films has been attempted using a variety of chemical and physical methods. However, the most frequently used deposition method has been metal–organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) and its variants, such as pulsed MOCVD. Although the MOCVD process has several advantages, such as improved ferroelectric reliability of the grown films (1), conformal deposition over 3-dimensional structures (2), and a self-regulation mechanism (3,4) by which the film cation composition ratio remains stoichiometric irrespective of the Pb and Ti precursor injection ratio, MOCVD showed several problems as a device size is scaled down to a design rule < ~ 200 nm. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) is generally characterized as having a unique self-regulated growth behavior due to its surface saturating growth mechanism (5).
